app.name: Vulnyard
app.description: Central repository scanning with Trivy and Dependency-Track

banner.configMissing_one: Missing configuration: {{variables}}. Scanning is disabled until you set the variable.
banner.configMissing_other: Missing configuration: {{variables}}. Scanning is disabled until you set the variables.
banner.trivyMissing: Trivy is not available. Install it with scripts/install-trivy.sh, or set TRIVY_BIN.
banner.gitMissing: git is not available in the application environment.
banner.authNone: The application runs with AUTH_MODE=none, so anyone who can reach it over the network has access. Run it behind a VPN or an authenticating reverse proxy.

status.error: Could not load the application status.

placeholder.title: Coming soon
placeholder.description: This part comes in a later milestone. The application skeleton is already running.

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.description: Vulnerability summary, trend and the riskiest projects. Counted from the default branch of each project.
dashboard.topProjectsEmpty: Nothing to show yet – no scanned project has findings.

trend.title: Findings trend
trend.empty: The trend appears once daily metric snapshots are available (the first one comes after the nightly run).

byTarget.title: By target
byTarget.description: A summary of each target and how the numbers changed over the last {{count}} days. Click a target to filter the trend chart.

projects.title: Projects
projects.emptyDescription: Loosen the filters, or add and run a scan target.
projects.excludedNotice: This project is excluded from scanning, so it does not count in the overview and is not added to runs.
projects.noFindings: Dependency-Track reports no findings for this project.
projects.notScannedYet: The project has not been scanned yet, so it has no findings.
projects.noHistory: This project has not been scanned yet.

override.title: Custom branch selection
override.none: The project follows the target settings.

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerabilities across projects grouped by CVE. Expand one to see everywhere we have it.
vulnerabilities.emptyDescription: Dependency-Track reports nothing for this filter.
vulnerabilities.notInOurProjects: Dependency-Track reports {{count}} affected projects, but none of them is ours.

threats.title: Threats
threats.description: Vulnerabilities in our projects that need attention first: exploited in the wild, likely to be exploited soon, or new and serious. Severity alone says how bad a vulnerability would be, not whether anybody uses it.

reasonHint.exploited: Listed in the CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities.
reasonHint.likely: EPSS of at least {{epss}}: the probability of exploitation in the next 30 days.
reasonHint.new: Critical or high, first seen in our projects in the last {{days}} days; a project's first scan does not count.

threats.newerVersion: A newer version of the component exists
threats.emptyDescription: Nothing in our projects is known to be exploited, likely to be exploited, or new and serious.

notice.kevDisabled: The CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities is turned off (KEV_FEED_URL is empty), so actively exploited vulnerabilities are not recognised.
notice.kevUnavailable: The CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities could not be downloaded, so actively exploited vulnerabilities are not recognised right now. The next attempt is within an hour.
notice.kevStale: The last update of the CISA catalog failed; the copy from {{date}} is used.
notice.epssMissing: Dependency-Track has no EPSS scores, so "likely to be exploited" stays empty. It stores them only with NVD vulnerabilities: turn on the NVD mirroring (Administration → Vulnerability Sources) and wait for its next run.
notice.kevSource: CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities: {{entries}} entries, released {{date}}.

targets.title: Scan targets
targets.description: Groups and projects to scan, including the branch selection and schedule.
targets.emptyDescription: Add a group or a project, choose branches and a schedule. The preview shows in advance what will be scanned.

form.searchFailed: Searching the source failed. Check the connection and the token.
form.name: Display name
form.nameHint: Optional – when empty, the name from the source is used.
form.branchModeDefaultHint: Each project is scanned on its default branch.
form.branchModeCustomHint: Branch names or glob patterns, for example main or release/*.
form.branchPatternsHint: Enter adds a pattern. For a project, the real branches are suggested.
form.maxBranchesHint: A safety net against a pattern that would match hundreds of branches. The default branch and the most recently committed branches come first.
form.cronCustomHint: A custom expression takes precedence over the preset. Five fields: minute hour day month day_of_week.
form.excludePatternsHint: A glob over the project path, for example sandbox/* or */archive-*.
form.skipUnchanged: Skip projects whose commit has not changed
form.webhookPlaceholder: empty = the global webhook is used
form.webhookHint: Optional. When set, notifications of this target go here instead of the global webhook – and they are sent even when notifications are disabled globally.
form.webhookStored: Stored: {{masked}}. An empty field keeps the current webhook; typing into the field and clearing it again removes the webhook.
form.credentialsHint: Empty = the instance and token from the environment ({{url}}). Fill in when the target is on another GitLab or should have its own token.
form.sourceTokenStored: stored – an empty field keeps the current token
form.sourceTokenHint: The token is stored in the database and never sent back to the browser. Required for a target on another instance.

preview.title: Project preview
preview.empty: Nothing would be scanned with these settings.

runs.title: Scan runs
runs.description: History of runs, their jobs and errors.
runs.emptyDescription: Start a scan of a target on the Scan targets page, or with the Scan everything button.
runs.noJobs: This run has no jobs – there was nothing to scan.
runs.forceHint: Forces a scan even of projects whose commit has not changed since the last scan.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Connection status, tool versions and global settings.
settings.timezoneHint: The time zone is set with the TZ variable.
settings.variablesHint: Only whether a variable is set is shown – the values are never sent anywhere.
settings.concurrencyHint: How many projects are scanned at the same time. Takes effect within a few seconds, running scans are not interrupted.
settings.defaultCronHint: Empty = new targets have no schedule, manual runs only.
settings.retentionHint: Runs and jobs older than this many days are deleted every night.
settings.globalExcludesHint: The patterns apply to every target, in addition to its own exclusions.
settings.dtrackUnsupported: unsupported version, {{minimum}} or newer is required

notifications.title: Chat notifications
notifications.description: After every scan that finds vulnerabilities, Vulnyard posts a message to Google Chat – with the repository, finding counts and maintainers.
notifications.webhookHint: Paste the incoming webhook address from Google Chat. It is stored in the database and only sent back to the browser shortened – it contains a key and a token, so the application never prints it.
notifications.webhookStored: Stored: {{masked}}. An empty field keeps the current webhook.
notifications.minSeverityHint: A message is sent only when the project has a finding of at least this severity.

ignores.title: Ignored vulnerabilities
ignores.description: Rules for vulnerabilities we will not act on. The suppression is sent to Dependency-Track too, so ignored findings count neither in the overview nor in notifications.
ignores.empty: No rules. A vulnerability can be ignored from the vulnerability summary, or with “Add rule”.
ignores.applyFailed: {{failed}} could not be sent to Dependency-Track.
ignores.confirmDelete: Delete the rule for {{vulnId}}? The suppression in Dependency-Track will be reverted.

form.title: Ignore rule
form.patternHelp: A glob over the component purl. “*” means any component, “pkg:npm/express@5.*” only express version 5.
form.expiresOnHelp: Optional. After this day the rule stops holding and the suppression is reverted.
form.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. does not affect us, waiting for an upstream fix…
form.reasonHelp: Written to the analysis comment in Dependency-Track.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: Tokens for other systems calling the Vulnyard API – for example an automation that creates a scan target when a new project appears. The token is sent in the Authorization: Bearer header. API documentation is at /api/docs.
tokens.confirmDelete: Delete token “{{name}}”? The system using it will lose access to the API.

form.name: Name
form.expiresOnHelp: Optional. Without a date it is valid until you delete it.

created.title: Token “{{name}}” has been created
created.once: Copy it now – you will not see it again. Only its fingerprint is stored.
